requirements.original: Concatenation operand: ?, ? length(0..infinity) or * length(0..infinity); Transformed string: *

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.11 -- Concatenation operand: ?, ? length(0..infinity) or * length(0..infinity); Transformed string: *

requirements.original: Concatenation operand: ? length(0) or * length(0); Transformed string: empty string
requirements.canonical: An operand `? length(0)` or `* length(0)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the empty string.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.11 -- Concatenation operand: ? length(0) or * length(0); Transformed string: empty string

requirements.canonical: An operand `? length(1)` or `* length(1)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "?".

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.11 -- Concatenation operand: ? length(1) or * length(1); Transformed string: "?"

requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from a character string template concatenation
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.11 -- Concatenation operand: ? length(1 .. infinity) or * length(1 .. infinity); Transformed string: "?+"

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.11 -- Concatenation operand: ? length(n .. infinity) or * length(n .. infinity); Transformed string: "?#(n,)"

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.11 -- Concatenation operand: ? length(n .. m) or * length(n .. m); Transformed string: "?#(n,m)"

requirements.original: Concatenation operand: pattern "content"; Transformed string: "content"
requirements.canonical: An operand `pattern "content"` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "content".
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from a character string template concatenation
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.11 -- Concatenation operand: pattern "content"; Transformed string: "content"

requirements.original: omit "(" TemplateInstance ")"
requirements.canonical: The `omit` operation has the syntax `omit` "(" TemplateInstance ")".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.12 -- omit "(" TemplateInstance ")"

requirements.original: A template with the omit restriction and with the same content as the operand, if the operand fulfils conditions of the omit template restriction as described in clause 15.8.
requirements.canonical: If the operand fulfils the conditions of the omit template restriction (clause 15.8), the `omit` operation IS returning a template with the omit restriction and with the same content as the operand.
requirements.condition: the operand fulfils the conditions of the omit template restriction
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.12 -- A template with the omit restriction and with the same content as the operand, if the operand fulfils conditions of the omit template restriction as described in clause 15.8.

requirements.original: Any other situation shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: If the operand does not fulfil the conditions of the omit template restriction, the `omit` operation SHALL cause an error.
requirements.condition: the operand does not fulfil the conditions of the omit template restriction
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.12 -- Any other situation shall cause an error.

requirements.original: NOTE: This means that the result of omit(m_myTemplate) can be safely assigned to templates with the omit restriction.
requirements.canonical: The result of the `omit` operation CAN be safely assigned to a template with the omit restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.12 -- NOTE: This means that the result of omit(m_myTemplate) can be safely assigned to templates with the omit restriction.

requirements.original: present "(" TemplateInstance ")"
requirements.canonical: The `present` operation has the syntax `present` "(" TemplateInstance ")".

examples.text: // definitions of restricted templates type record ExampleType { integer a, boolean b optional } template ExampleType m_originalOmit := omit; template ExampleType m_originalValue := { 1, true}; template ExampleType m_originalAny := ?; template(present) ExampleType m_targetOmit := present(m_riginalOmit); //causes error template(present) ExampleType m_targetValue:= present(m_originalValue); template(present) ExampleType m_targetAny := present(m_originalAny);

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.13 -- present "(" TemplateInstance ")"

requirements.original: A template with the present restriction and with the same content as the operand, if the operand fulfils conditions of the present template restriction as described in clause 15.8.
requirements.canonical: If the operand fulfils the conditions of the present template restriction (clause 15.8), the `present` operation IS returning a template with the present restriction and with the same content as the operand.
requirements.condition: the operand fulfils the conditions of the present template restriction

examples.text: // definitions of restricted templates type record ExampleType { integer a, boolean b optional } template ExampleType m_originalOmit := omit; template ExampleType m_originalValue := { 1, true}; template ExampleType m_originalAny := ?; template(present) ExampleType m_targetOmit := present(m_riginalOmit); //causes error template(present) ExampleType m_targetValue:= present(m_originalValue); template(present) ExampleType m_targetAny := present(m_originalAny);

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.13 -- A template with the present restriction and with the same content as the operand, if the operand fulfils conditions of the present template restriction as described in clause 15.8.

requirements.original: Any other situation shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: If the operand does not fulfil the conditions of the present template restriction, the `present` operation SHALL cause an error.
requirements.condition: the operand does not fulfil the conditions of the present template restriction

examples.text: // definitions of restricted templates type record ExampleType { integer a, boolean b optional } template ExampleType m_originalOmit := omit; template ExampleType m_originalValue := { 1, true}; template ExampleType m_originalAny := ?; template(present) ExampleType m_targetOmit := present(m_riginalOmit); //causes error template(present) ExampleType m_targetValue:= present(m_originalValue); template(present) ExampleType m_targetAny := present(m_originalAny);

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.13 -- Any other situation shall cause an error.

requirements.original: NOTE: This means that the result of present(m_myTemplate) can be safely assigned to templates with the present restriction.
requirements.canonical: The result of the `present` operation CAN be safely assigned to a template with the present restriction.

examples.text: // definitions of restricted templates type record ExampleType { integer a, boolean b optional } template ExampleType m_originalOmit := omit; template ExampleType m_originalValue := { 1, true}; template ExampleType m_originalAny := ?; template(present) ExampleType m_targetOmit := present(m_riginalOmit); //causes error template(present) ExampleType m_targetValue:= present(m_originalValue); template(present) ExampleType m_targetAny := present(m_originalAny);

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.13 -- NOTE: This means that the result of present(m_myTemplate) can be safely assigned to templates with the present restriction.

requirements.original: The conversion of a general (unrestricted) template to a template with the present restriction can be achieved by applying the .present notation to the template.
requirements.canonical: The presentness conversion IS the application of the `.present` notation to a general (unrestricted) template, converting it to a template with the present restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.14 -- The conversion of a general (unrestricted) template to a template with the present restriction can be achieved by applying the .present notation to the template.

requirements.original: TemplateInstance "." present
requirements.canonical: The presentness conversion has the syntax TemplateInstance "." `present`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.14 -- TemplateInstance "." present

requirements.original: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with no restriction yields a template with the present restriction with the following content:
requirements.canonical: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with no template restriction IS yielding a template with the present restriction.
requirements.condition: the template expression has no template restriction
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.14 -- Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with no restriction yields a template with the present restriction with the following content:

requirements.original: _AnyValue if the referenced template contained AnyValueOrNone._
requirements.canonical: If the unrestricted template referenced by the presentness conversion contains AnyValueOrNone, the presentness conversion IS yielding AnyValue.
requirements.condition: the referenced unrestricted template contains AnyValueOrNone

readings: If the referenced template is AnyValueOrNone at its top level, the presentness conversion yields AnyValue.
Every AnyValueOrNone contained anywhere in the referenced template (including nested fields) is replaced by AnyValue.
ambiguity.issue: 'contained' does not state whether only the top-level matching mechanism or also nested fields are affected; the top-level reading is assumed, consistent with the present restriction applying to the top level only (clause 15.8).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.14 -- _AnyValue if the referenced template contained AnyValueOrNone._

requirements.original: Matching mechanism without the ifpresent attribute if the referenced template had this attribute attached to it.
requirements.canonical: If the matching mechanism of the unrestricted template referenced by the presentness conversion has the `ifpresent` attribute attached, the presentness conversion IS yielding the same matching mechanism without the `ifpresent` attribute.
requirements.condition: the referenced template has the ifpresent attribute attached
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.14 -- Matching mechanism without the ifpresent attribute if the referenced template had this attribute attached to it.

requirements.original: _TemplateList where all the alternatives that evaluate to omit are removed and the presentness conversion is_ applied to all other alternatives.
requirements.canonical: If the unrestricted template referenced by the presentness conversion is a template list, the presentness conversion IS yielding the template list with all alternatives that evaluate to `omit` removed and with the presentness conversion applied to all other alternatives.
requirements.condition: the referenced template is a template list
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.14 -- _TemplateList where all the alternatives that evaluate to omit are removed and the presentness conversion is_ applied to all other alternatives.

requirements.original: Unchanged template in all other cases.
requirements.canonical: In all cases other than AnyValueOrNone, a matching mechanism with `ifpresent` and a template list, the presentness conversion of an unrestricted template IS yielding the unchanged template.
requirements.condition: none of the other conversion cases applies
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.14 -- Unchanged template in all other cases.

requirements.original: NOTE: Other matching attributes such as length are unaffected by the conversion, e.g. * length(2..10) would be converted to ? length(2..10)
requirements.canonical: A matching attribute other than `ifpresent`, such as a length restriction, IS NOT affected by the presentness conversion (e.g. `* length(2..10)` is converted to `? length(2..10)`).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.14 -- NOTE: Other matching attributes such as length are unaffected by the conversion, e.g. * length(2..10) would be converted to ? length(2..10)

requirements.original: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression that has the present or value restriction yields the same template with the same template restriction.
requirements.canonical: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with the present or value restriction IS yielding the same template with the same template restriction.
requirements.condition: the template expression has the present or value restriction
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.14 -- Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression that has the present or value restriction yields the same template with the same template restriction.

requirements.original: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with the omit template restriction yields the same template with the value restriction.
requirements.canonical: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with the omit template restriction IS yielding the same template with the value restriction.
requirements.condition: the template expression has the omit restriction
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.14 -- Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with the omit template restriction yields the same template with the value restriction.

requirements.original: a) Applying the presentness conversion to a template that only matches the special value omit shall result in an error.
requirements.canonical: Applying the presentness conversion to a template that only matches the special value `omit` SHALL result in an error.
requirements.condition: the template only matches omit
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.14 -- a) Applying the presentness conversion to a template that only matches the special value omit shall result in an error.

requirements.original: The extraction of the underlying value from a charstring pattern matching mechanism or a template with the omit restriction can be achieved with the .value notation applied to a TemplateInstance.
requirements.canonical: The value extraction IS the application of the `.value` notation to a template instance, extracting the underlying value from a `charstring` pattern matching mechanism or from a template with the omit restriction.

readings: The value extraction applies only to `charstring` patterns and to templates with the omit restriction.

The value extraction applies to any template instance that contains a pattern, a value with `ifpresent`, or a value (as stated in the Semantic Description and Restrictions), irrespective of its template restriction.
ambiguity.issue: The introductory sentence limits the operand to charstring patterns and omit-restricted templates, while 15.15-s005..s008 and the example (an unrestricted var template with ifpresent) accept any template containing a value; the broader second reading is assumed in the other requirements, the first is used here as stated.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.15 -- The extraction of the underlying value from a charstring pattern matching mechanism or a template with the omit restriction can be achieved with the .value notation applied to a TemplateInstance.

requirements.original: TemplateInstance "." value
requirements.canonical: The value extraction has the syntax TemplateInstance "." `value`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.15 -- TemplateInstance "." value

requirements.original: Applying this extraction to a pattern matching mechanism of the form pattern _StringValue will yield the value_ _StringValue.
requirements.canonical: Applying the value extraction to a pattern matching mechanism of the form `pattern` StringValue IS yielding the value StringValue.
requirements.condition: the operand is a pattern of the form pattern StringValue
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.15 -- Applying this extraction to a pattern matching mechanism of the form pattern _StringValue will yield the value_ _StringValue.

requirements.original: If the pattern contains any matching attribute, the attribute shall be removed by the extraction._
requirements.canonical: If the pattern operand of the value extraction contains any matching attribute, the value extraction SHALL remove that attribute.
requirements.condition: the pattern contains a matching attribute
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.15 -- If the pattern contains any matching attribute, the attribute shall be removed by the extraction._

requirements.original: Applying this extraction to a template that evaluates to Value `ifpresent will yield the value Value.`
requirements.canonical: Applying the value extraction to a template that evaluates to Value `ifpresent` IS yielding the value Value.
requirements.condition: the template evaluates to Value ifpresent
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.15 -- Applying this extraction to a template that evaluates to Value `ifpresent will yield the value Value.`

requirements.original: Applying this extraction to a template that contains a value will yield that value.
requirements.canonical: Applying the value extraction to a template that contains a value IS yielding that value.
requirements.condition: the template contains a value
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.15 -- Applying this extraction to a template that contains a value will yield that value.

requirements.original: a) Applying the value extraction to a template that contains neither a pattern nor a value template with an ifpresent matching attribute nor a value shall result in an error.
requirements.canonical: Applying the value extraction to a template that contains neither a pattern, nor a value template with an `ifpresent` matching attribute, nor a value SHALL result in an error.
requirements.condition: the template contains neither a pattern, nor a value with ifpresent, nor a value
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.15 -- a) Applying the value extraction to a template that contains neither a pattern nor a value template with an ifpresent matching attribute nor a value shall result in an error.

requirements.canonical: A function definition has the syntax `function` [`@deterministic` | `@control`] (FunctionIdentifier | `control`) "(" [{(FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar) [","]}] ")" [`runs on` ComponentType] [`mtc` ComponentType] [`system` ComponentType] [`return` [TemplateModifier] TypeOrNestedTypeDef [ArrayDef]] StatementBlock.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- function [ @deterministic | @control ] ( FunctionIdentifier | control ) "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")" [ runs on ComponentType ] [ mtc ComponentType ] [ system ComponentType ] [ return [ TemplateModifier ] TypeOrNestedTypeDef [ArrayDef] ] StatementBlock

requirements.canonical: A function definition MAY carry at most one of the modifiers `@deterministic` and `@control`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- function [ @deterministic | @control ] ( FunctionIdentifier | control ) "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")" [ runs on ComponentType ] [ mtc ComponentType ] [ system ComponentType ] [ return [ TemplateModifier ] TypeOrNestedTypeDef [ArrayDef] ] StatementBlock

requirements.canonical: The `runs on`, `mtc`, `system` and `return` clauses of a function definition are optional and, when present, appear in this order before the statement block.

requirements.original: Functions may return a value or a template.
requirements.canonical: A function MAY return a value or a template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- Functions may return a value or a template.

requirements.original: Value return is denoted by the return keyword followed by a type expression.
requirements.canonical: A value return IS denoted in the function header by the `return` keyword followed by a type expression.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- Value return is denoted by the return keyword followed by a type expression.

requirements.original: Template return is denoted by the return keywords followed by a TemplateModifier and a type expression.
requirements.canonical: A template return IS denoted in the function header by the `return` keyword followed by a TemplateModifier and a type expression.

ambiguity.issue: The plural 'return keywords' is used although only the single `return` keyword is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- Template return is denoted by the return keywords followed by a TemplateModifier and a type expression.

requirements.original: Execution of a return statement in the body of the function causes evaluation of the return value or template, the function to terminate and to return the result to the location of the call of the function.
requirements.canonical: Execution of a return statement in the body of a function evaluates the return value or template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- Execution of a return statement in the body of the function causes evaluation of the return value or template, the function to terminate and to return the result to the location of the call of the function.

requirements.original: Execution of a return statement in the body of the function causes evaluation of the return value or template, the function to terminate and to return the result to the location of the call of the function.
requirements.canonical: Execution of a return statement in the body of a function terminates the function.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- Execution of a return statement in the body of the function causes evaluation of the return value or template, the function to terminate and to return the result to the location of the call of the function.

requirements.original: Execution of a return statement in the body of the function causes evaluation of the return value or template, the function to terminate and to return the result to the location of the call of the function.
requirements.canonical: Execution of a return statement in the body of a function returns the result to the location of the call of the function.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- Execution of a return statement in the body of the function causes evaluation of the return value or template, the function to terminate and to return the result to the location of the call of the function.

requirements.original: Functions may be parameterized.
requirements.canonical: A function MAY be parameterized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- Functions may be parameterized.

requirements.original: Functions may have an mtc clause.
requirements.canonical: A function MAY have an mtc clause.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- Functions may have an mtc clause.

requirements.original: If a function has an mtc clause, the type referenced by this clause shall be mtccompatible (see clause 6.3.2.7) with the type of the mtc component reference.
requirements.canonical: If a function has an mtc clause, the component type referenced by the mtc clause SHALL be mtc-compatible with the type of the mtc component reference.
requirements.condition: the function has an mtc clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- If a function has an mtc clause, the type referenced by this clause shall be mtccompatible (see clause 6.3.2.7) with the type of the mtc component reference.

requirements.original: If the mtc clause is not present, the type of the mtc component reference is unknown in the scope of this function.
requirements.canonical: If a function has no mtc clause, the type of the mtc component reference IS unknown in the scope of the function.
requirements.condition: the mtc clause is not present
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- If the mtc clause is not present, the type of the mtc component reference is unknown in the scope of this function.

requirements.original: Functions may have a system clause.
requirements.canonical: A function MAY have a system clause.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- Functions may have a system clause.

requirements.original: If a function has a system clause, the type referenced by this clause shall be system-compatible (see clause 6.3.2.7) with the type of the system component reference.
requirements.canonical: If a function has a system clause, the component type referenced by the system clause SHALL be system-compatible with the type of the system component reference.
requirements.condition: the function has a system clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- If a function has a system clause, the type referenced by this clause shall be system-compatible (see clause 6.3.2.7) with the type of the system component reference.

requirements.original: If the system clause is not present, the type of the system component reference is unknown in the scope of this function.
requirements.canonical: If a function has no system clause, the type of the system component reference IS unknown in the scope of the function.
requirements.condition: the system clause is not present
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- If the system clause is not present, the type of the system component reference is unknown in the scope of this function.

requirements.original: Using the @deterministic modifier, a function can be declared to be deterministic.
requirements.canonical: A function MAY be declared deterministic by using the `@deterministic` modifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- Using the @deterministic modifier, a function can be declared to be deterministic.

requirements.original: a) A function without runs on clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a runs on clause locally.
requirements.canonical: A function without a `runs on` clause SHALL NOT locally invoke a function that has a `runs on` clause.
requirements.condition: the function has no runs on clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- a) A function without runs on clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a runs on clause locally.

requirements.original: a) A function without runs on clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a runs on clause locally.
requirements.canonical: A function without a `runs on` clause SHALL NOT locally invoke an altstep that has a `runs on` clause.
requirements.condition: the function has no runs on clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- a) A function without runs on clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a runs on clause locally.

requirements.original: a) A function without runs on clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a runs on clause locally.
requirements.canonical: A function without a `runs on` clause SHALL NOT activate as default an altstep that has a `runs on` clause.
requirements.condition: the function has no runs on clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- a) A function without runs on clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a runs on clause locally.

requirements.original: b) Functions started by using the start test component operation shall always have a runs on clause (see clause 22.5) and are considered to be invoked in the component to be started, i.e. not locally.
requirements.canonical: A function started by the start test component operation SHALL have a `runs on` clause.
requirements.condition: the function is started with the start test component operation
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- b) Functions started by using the start test component operation shall always have a runs on clause (see clause 22.5) and are considered to be invoked in the component to be started, i.e. not locally.

requirements.original: However, the start test component operation may be invoked within behaviour without a runs `on clause.`
requirements.canonical: The start test component operation MAY be invoked within behaviour without a `runs on` clause.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- However, the start test component operation may be invoked within behaviour without a runs `on clause.`

requirements.original: c) Functions called directly or indirectly from a module control function shall have no mtc or system clause.
requirements.canonical: A function called directly or indirectly from a module control function SHALL NOT have an mtc clause or a system clause.
requirements.condition: the function is called directly or indirectly from a module control function
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- c) Functions called directly or indirectly from a module control function shall have no mtc or system clause.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: Nevertheless, functions called directly or indirectly from the module control function are allowed to execute test cases.
requirements.canonical: A function called directly or indirectly from the module control function MAY execute testcases.

ambiguity.issue: 'test cases' is used for the TTCN-3 language element 'testcase'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- NOTE 2: Nevertheless, functions called directly or indirectly from the module control function are allowed to execute test cases.

requirements.original: d) The rules for formal parameter lists shall be followed as defined in clause 5.4.
requirements.canonical: The formal parameter list of a function SHALL follow the rules for formal parameter lists defined in clause 5.4.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- d) The rules for formal parameter lists shall be followed as defined in clause 5.4.

requirements.original: e) For return TemplateModifier statements the restrictions specified in clause 15.0 shall apply.
requirements.canonical: A return clause with a TemplateModifier SHALL obey the restrictions specified in clause 15.0.

improper_terms.proper: return clause with a template modifier

ambiguity.issue: The text speaks of 'statements', but the return TemplateModifier construct is part of the function header return clause, not a statement.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.0 -- e) For return TemplateModifier statements the restrictions specified in clause 15.0 shall apply.
